meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to see each other, to meet
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see each other', paired with 'увидеться'.

examples.trans: We haven't seen each other in a hundred years!

examples.text: Слушай, ну сто лет не виделись, да?
examples.trans: Listen, we haven't seen each other in a hundred years, right?
She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выписать.gloss: to issue, to make out (a document)

meanings.note: An order, receipt, prescription. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'писать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to issue, to make out (a document)', paired with 'выписывать'.

examples.trans: The occupancy order is made out to Samsonov.
The doctor wrote out a prescription.

examples.text: Ордер выписан на Самсонова Ивана Васильевича. Ну, что скажете, друзья?
examples.trans: The occupancy order is made out to Samsonov Ivan Vasilyevich. Well, what do you say, my friends?

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'nursery / kids' room' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is making the nursery room for us.

examples.text: А хотите посмотреть, как мы детскую сделали?
examples.trans: And would you like to see how we redid the nursery?

meanings.note: For or belonging to children. Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('children's, childish').
Детский лепет = baby talk. Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('children's, childish').

examples.text: Мучить? Детские слова какие. Ну давай, мучай, Самсон!
examples.trans: Torture? What childish words. Go on then, torture me, Samson!

meanings.note: affectionate form of дочь; also used by older people to address a young woman

examples.text: Мой Гриша мечтать об этом не мог! Спасибо, дочка!
examples.trans: My Grisha could not even dream of this! Thank you, dear!

ездить.gloss: to go (by vehicle, habitually or round-trip)

meanings.en: to go by vehicle, to travel (habitually or there and back)
meanings.note: Multidirectional partner of ехать. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle, habitually or round-trip)', paired with 'ехать'.

examples.text: И в сауну я не езжу.
examples.trans: And I don't go to saunas.
We often go to the seaside.

examples.text: Послушайте, Артурик, я уже давно не танцую. И в сауну я не езжу.
examples.trans: Listen, Arturik, I haven't danced in a long time. And I don't go to saunas.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement
забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Запретить кому + infinitive. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forbid, to ban', paired with 'запрещать'.

examples.trans: The doctor forbade him to drink.

examples.text: Аникеев же запретил! Нам нельзя пить.
examples.trans: But Anikeev forbade it! We mustn't drink.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'forbid'.

examples.trans: I forbid you! Where are you going?

examples.text: Нет, это глупо и опасно. Я тебе запрещаю.
examples.trans: No, this is foolish and dangerous. I forbid you.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

Кажется as a parenthetical word. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to seem', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'baby crib, cot' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть кроватка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always baby crib.

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Всё получилось = it all worked out. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: the person helped is in the dative: 'помогать маме' = to help mum

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Я прекрасно понимаю = I understand perfectly
As a reply. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Нет, лучше так: все говорят, а я делаю! Прекрасно.
examples.trans: No, better like this: everyone talks, while I do! Excellent.

meanings.note: Informal: family and friends. Core Russian interj meaning 'hi' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Рано умер = died young / too early. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Муж тоже там работал. И рано умер.
examples.trans: My husband worked there too. And he died young.
Tomorrow I need to get up early.

examples.text: Что, по домам? Мне завтра рано вставать.
examples.trans: What, time to go home? I have to get up early tomorrow.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'maternity hospital' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В моём районе есть один неплохой роддом.
examples.trans: In my neighborhood there is a pretty good maternity hospital.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть роддом.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always maternity hospital.

meanings.en: dear, darling, my friend (in address: родной мой)
meanings.note: Often used ironically. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('native, own; dear, darling').
родной брат = full brother; родной город = hometown

examples.text: Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: Well then, my dear friend, to you!

examples.text: Это будущий мэр Синеозерска! Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: That is the future mayor of Sineozersk! Well then, my dear friend, to you!

meanings.note: Adverb. Core Russian adv meaning 'nearby, next to' in everyday speech.
Рядом с + instrumental. Core Russian adv meaning 'nearby, next to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café.

examples.text: Теперь меня рядом с ним похоронить не хотят!
examples.trans: Now they won't even bury me next to him!

examples.text: Тут рядом, за углом, чебуречная. Там нормально.
examples.trans: Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café. It's fine there.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Так, семья Самсоновых. Он строитель, она медсестра.
examples.trans: Right, the Samsonov family. He's a builder, she's a nurse.

meanings.note: Медсестра; also медицинская сестра. Common feminine noun meaning 'sister' in everyday Russian.
Медсестра; also медицинская сестра. Common feminine noun meaning 'sister' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He gave our sister a flat.

examples.text: Ты бы брал пример с сестры! Сестра умная, серьёзная, старательная.
examples.trans: You should follow your sister's example! Your sister is smart, serious, and hardworking.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to plan, to be going to
meanings.note: + infinitive. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

Pack or assemble. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('assembled').

examples.trans: Thank you for the assembled baby crib.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень собранный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very assembled choice.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Possession. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Утром = in the morning. Common neuter noun meaning 'morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
